entries.name: Zao Terrace 凿台
entries.note: a terrace at Yuci (Xu Guang), by the Dongguo River (Zhengyi).

entries.name: Sui River 随水
entries.note: the river at Sui; modern Suizhou, Hubei.

entries.name: Liu 留
entries.note: modern Pei County, Jiangsu.

entries.name: Fangyu 方与
entries.note: modern Yutai, Shandong.

entries.name: Zhi 铚
entries.note: modern Suzhou (宿州), Anhui.

entries.name: Huling 湖陵
entries.note: south-east of modern Yutai, Shandong.

entries.name: Dang 砀
entries.note: modern Dangshan, Anhui.

entries.name: Xiao 萧
entries.note: modern Xiao County, Anhui.

entries.name: Xiang 相
entries.note: modern Suixi, Anhui.

entries.name: the Si country 泗上
entries.note: the lands along the Si River, between Lu and Chu.

entries.name: the River 河
entries.note: the Yellow River.

entries.name: the eastern mountains 东山
entries.note: the mountains east of Qin's passes, the Xiao range.

entries.name: Zheng 郑
entries.note: the capital of Han; modern Xinzheng, Henan.

entries.name: Xu 许
entries.note: modern Xuchang, Henan.

entries.name: Yanling 鄢陵
entries.note: modern Yanling, Henan.

entries.name: Shangcai 上蔡
entries.note: modern Shangcai, Henan.

entries.name: Shaoling 召陵
entries.note: modern Luohe, Henan.

entries.name: the land north of the Huai 淮北
entries.note: Chu's lands north of the Huai River; northern Anhui and Jiangsu.

entries.name: Jiangdong 江东
entries.note: the lands east of the lower Yangtze; southern Jiangsu.

entries.name: Lanling 兰陵
entries.note: modern Lanling County, Shandong.

entries.name: the upper lands 上地
entries.note: Han's highland territory towards Shangdang, in south-eastern Shanxi.

pages.label: 255 BC · Ivar the Boneless' commentary and analysis II

entries.name: Wucheng 吴城
entries.note: a Wei town in Dayang (Xu Guang); the old city of Yu on Yu Mountain, also called Wu Mountain, fifty li north-east of Hebei County in Shanzhou (Zhengyi, citing the Kuodi zhi); modern Pinglu County, Shanxi.

entries.name: Shuzhou 徐州
entries.note: east of Lu, the Xue County of Han times (Xu Guang); the Shuowen writes it 䣄, and the Suoyin gives its pronunciation as that of 舒, shu; modern Tengzhou, Shandong.

entries.name: Yong 雍
entries.note: the old capital of Qin and seat of its altars; modern Fengxiang, Baoji, Shaanxi.

entries.name: Juyang 鉅陽
entries.note: Chu's seat after Chen; identified with the Diandingzi walled site at Juyang village, Gongji, in Taihe County, Anhui, on the Xifei River.

entries.name: Songzi 宋子
entries.note: a Zhao town; Xu Guang: in Julu; north-east of modern Zhao County, Hebei.

entries.name: Weiwen 尉文
entries.note: the fief granted to Lian Po; the Suoyin: probably a place name, or else 尉 an office and 文 a name; the Zhengyi: probably land in Weizhou (modern Yu County, Hebei).

entries.name: Dongwucheng 东武城
entries.note: Lord Pingyuan's fief; Xu Guang: in Qinghe; the Zhengyi: Wucheng County in Beizhou; modern Wucheng, Shandong.

entries.name: Yiling 夷陵
entries.note: the burial ground of the kings of Chu; modern Yichang, Hubei.

entries.name: Li 李
entries.note: the fief of Li Tong's father; Xu Guang: Li city in Chenggao in Henei; the Zhengyi: Wen County in Huaizhou was originally Li city; modern Wen County, Henan.

entries.name: Fanyang 繁阳
entries.note: a Wei town; Xu Guang: in Wei Commandery; the Zhengyi: north-east of Neihuang County in Xiangzhou; modern Neihuang, Henan.

entries.name: Eastern Zhou 东周
entries.note: the Eastern Zhou domain, the eastern of the two fiefs into which the Zhou royal house was divided, centred on Gong (modern Gongyi, Henan).

entries.name: Chenggao 成皋
entries.note: a Han town; the Zhengyi: the old Eastern Guo, Zheng's town of Zhi, also called Hulao, the Han dynasty's Chenggao; north-west of modern Xingyang, Henan.

entries.name: Gong 巩
entries.note: a Han town; the Zhengyi: Gong County in Luozhou; modern Gongyi, Henan.

entries.name: Yangren 阳人
entries.note: Xu Guang: the Yangren settlement in Liang County of Henan; the Zhengyi: the old Yangren city forty li west of Liang County in Ruzhou; west of modern Ruzhou, Henan.

entries.name: Sanchuan Commandery 三川郡
entries.note: a Qin Commandery, named for its three rivers, the Yellow River, Luo River and Yi River (Wei Zhao); established in 249 BC on the lands of Zhou and Han around Luoyang; renamed Henan Commandery under the Han (Pei Yin).

entries.name: Xingyang 荥阳
entries.note: a Han town east of Chenggao; modern Xingyang, Henan.

entries.name: Bian 卞
entries.note: a Lu town; east of modern Sishui, Shandong.

entries.name: Ke 柯
entries.note: a Qi settlement; the Suoyin cites Du Yu, now Dong'e in Jibei; the old Dong'e city, south-east of modern Yanggu, Shandong.

entries.name: Henan 河南
entries.note: the Han name of Sanchuan Commandery, the lands around Luoyang; the Shiji uses it of Qin's commandery (Suoyin).

entries.name: Luoyang 雒阳
entries.note: the old Zhou capital on the Luo; modern Luoyang, Henan.

entries.name: Langya 琅琊
entries.note: the seat of the kings of Yue after Goujian; placed by tradition at the Langya of Shandong (modern Jiaonan, Qingdao), and by the report cited here at Jinpingshan, Lianyungang, Jiangsu. Written 瑯琊 and 琅邪 as well.

entries.name: Jiang 江
entries.note: the Yangtze.

entries.name: Huai 淮
entries.note: the Huai River.

entries.name: Jin 晋
entries.note: the state of Jin, in modern Shanxi, from which Han, Zhao and Wei were formed.

entries.name: Wu Commandery 吴郡
entries.note: the Han Commandery of Wu, around modern Suzhou, Jiangsu.

entries.name: An County 安县
entries.note: a County of Wu Commandery under the Han, listed in the Xu Hanshu's Treatise on Commanderies and Kingdoms; north of modern Jiaxing, Zhejiang.

entries.name: Xicen tomb 西岑冢
entries.note: a tomb in Wu Commandery named in the Yuejue.

entries.name: Jinpingshan 锦屏山
entries.note: a hill at Lianyungang, Jiangsu, formerly Qushan and Langyashan, with the walled site at Jiulongkou.

entries.name: Qushan 朐山
entries.note: the earlier name of Jinpingshan at Lianyungang, Jiangsu.

entries.name: Qu County 朐县
entries.note: the Qin County at Qushan; modern Lianyungang, Jiangsu.

entries.name: Langya Terrace 琅琊台
entries.note: the terrace raised by the First Emperor of Qin on the coast of Langya; modern Jiaonan, Qingdao, Shandong.

entries.name: Fengtian 奉天
entries.note: Fengtian in pinyin, Hōten in Japanese reading; the Mukden of the Western press of the day. The seat of the Fengtian clique; modern Shenyang, Liaoning.

entries.name: Shimenzi 石門子
entries.note: Shimenzi in pinyin, Sekimonshi in Japanese reading: the Shimenzhai 石門寨 of the Chinese accounts, in the hills north-west of Shanhai Pass; modern Shimenzhai, Qinhuangdao, Hebei.

entries.name: Jinzhou 錦州
entries.note: Jinzhou in pinyin, Kinshū in Japanese reading; a city of western Fengtian province; modern Jinzhou, Liaoning.

entries.name: Qingdao 青島
entries.note: Qingdao in pinyin, Chintao in Japanese reading; the port on the Shandong coast; modern Qingdao.

entries.name: Qinhuangdao 秦皇島
entries.note: Qinhuangdao in pinyin, Shinkōtō in Japanese reading; the port on the Bohai coast west of Shanhai Pass; modern Qinhuangdao, Hebei.

entries.name: Shanhai Pass 山海關
entries.note: Shanhaiguan in pinyin, Sankaikan in Japanese reading; the Pass where the Great Wall meets the sea, on the road from Hebei into Manchuria; modern Shanhaiguan, Qinhuangdao, Hebei.

entries.name: Tianjin 天津
entries.note: Tianjin in pinyin, Tenshin in Japanese reading; the port city on the Hai River; modern Tianjin.

entries.name: Beijing 北京
entries.note: Beijing in pinyin, Pekin in Japanese reading; the capital of the Republic in 1924; modern Beijing.

entries.name: Ju 沮
entries.note: a County of Qin in Hanzhong Commandery, on the upper Ju River 沮水 (the Jialing); modern Lueyang 略阳, Shaanxi.

pages.label: 249 BC · Qin slips in the Yuelu Academy collection

entries.name: Nanzheng 南郑
entries.note: a County of Qin, the seat of Hanzhong Commandery, in the Han River valley; modern Hanzhong 汉中, Shaanxi.

pages.label: 249 BC · Qin slips in the Yuelu Academy collection

entries.name: Suxu 宿胥
entries.note: a place on the Yellow River in Wei, Suxu Mouth 宿胥口, where the river's old course turned north; modern Xun County 浚县, Henan.

pages.label: 249 BC · Appendix: text of the Zhanguo Zonghengjia Shu

entries.name: Kuaiji 会稽
entries.note: the mountain in Yue on which King Goujian was besieged by Wu in 494 BC; modern Shaoxing, Zhejiang.

pages.label: 249 BC · Appendix: text of the Zhanguo Zonghengjia Shu

entries.name: Yinjin 阴晋
entries.note: a town of Wei on the Qin border east of the Hua mountain, taken by Qin in 332 BC and renamed Ningqin 宁秦; modern Huayin 华阴, Shaanxi.

pages.label: 249 BC · Appendix: text of the Zhanguo Zonghengjia Shu

entries.name: Shangluo 上雒
entries.note: a County of Qin on the upper Luo River, on the road from the Guanzhong to Nanyang; modern Shangluo 商洛, Shaanxi.

pages.label: 249 BC · Appendix: text of the Zhanguo Zonghengjia Shu

entries.name: Taiyuan 太原
entries.note: the basin of the middle Fen River, Zhao's north-western region, made a Commandery of Qin; modern Taiyuan, Shanxi.

entries.name: Xincheng 新城
entries.note: a city of Zhao, also called Xiaopingcheng 小平城; the Zhengyi places it forty-seven li south-west of Shanyang County in Shuozhou; modern Shuozhou 朔州, Shanxi.

entries.name: Langmeng 狼孟
entries.note: a city of Zhao north of Jinyang, later a County of Taiyuan Commandery (Jijie); modern Yangqu 阳曲, Shanxi.

entries.name: Gaodu 高都
entries.note: a city of Wei in the hills south of Shangdang; the Zhengyi: its old city is Zezhou; modern Jincheng 晋城, Shanxi.

entries.name: Ji 汲
entries.note: a city of Wei in Henei, north of the Yellow River; the Zhengyi: its old city twenty-five li south-west of Ji County in Weizhou; modern Weihui 卫辉, Henan.

entries.name: Shangdang 上党
entries.note: the upland region between the Taihang and the Fen, held in parts by Han and Zhao and contested with Qin; modern Changzhi 长治, Shanxi.

entries.name: Longdui 龙兑
entries.note: a town of Zhao on the Yan border; the Zhengyi takes it from the Longshan of the Kuodizhi, twenty-five li south-west of Suicheng County in Yizhou; modern Xushui 徐水, Hebei.

entries.name: Fenmen 汾门
entries.note: a town of Zhao on the Yan border; the Jijie (Xu Guang): in Beixincheng; the Zhengyi suspects 汾 an error for the Longmen gorge of the Xu River, in the lands of Suicheng, Yongle, Gu'an and Xincheng; modern Xushui 徐水, Hebei.

entries.name: Linle 临乐
entries.note: a town of Zhao on the Yan border; the Jijie: Fangcheng has a Linxiang; the Zhengyi: the old city of Linxiang seventeen li south of Gu'an in Youzhou; modern Gu'an 固安, Hebei.

entries.name: Ge 葛
entries.note: a town of Yan; the Jijie: Gecheng in Gaoyang; the Zhengyi: also called Xihe city, fifty li north-west of Gaoyang County in Yingzhou; modern Gaoyang 高阳, Hebei.

entries.name: Wuyang 武阳
entries.note: the lower capital of Yan 燕下都 on the Yi River; modern Yixian 易县, Hebei.

entries.name: Pingshu 平舒
entries.note: a town of Yan; the Jijie: in Dai Commandery; the Zhengyi: its old city ninety-three li north of Lingqiu County in Weizhou; modern Guangling 广灵, Shanxi.

entries.name: Rong 戎
entries.note: the lands of the Rong peoples west of Qin; the Western Rong 西戎 of Duke Mu's hegemony.

entries.name: Wan 宛
entries.note: a city of Chu on the upper Han; modern Nanyang 南阳, Henan.

entries.name: Ba 巴
entries.note: the state and region of Ba on the upper Yangtze, taken by Qin in 316 BC; modern Chongqing.

entries.name: Shu 蜀
entries.note: the state and region of Shu, the Chengdu plain, taken by Qin in 316 BC; the 西蜀 of the memorial.

entries.name: Shang Commandery 上郡
entries.note: the Commandery north of the Wei on the Luo, ceded by Wei to Qin; the Zhengyi: fifteen Counties, in King Huiwen's tenth year; modern northern Shaanxi.

entries.name: Hanzhong 汉中
entries.note: the upper Han valley, taken from Chu by Qin; the Zhengyi: six hundred li, in King Huiwen's thirteenth year; modern Hanzhong, Shaanxi.

entries.name: Jiangnan 江南
entries.note: the lands south of the Yangtze.

entries.name: Taishan 太山
entries.note: Mount Tai 泰山, written 太山; modern Tai'an, Shandong.

entries.name: Kunshan 昆山
entries.note: the jade mountain of the far west; the Zhengyi: Kun'gang, four hundred li north-east of Khotan.

entries.name: Sui 随
entries.note: the state of Sui on the Han, of the pearl of Marquis Sui; modern Suizhou, Hubei.

entries.name: E 阿
entries.note: Dong'e 东阿 of Qi, source of fine silk (Jijie); modern Yanggu, Shandong.

entries.name: Sangjian 桑间
entries.note: a place on the Pu River in Wey, proverbial for its licentious music.

entries.name: Pinglu 平陆
entries.note: a town on Qi's western border (Suoyin), a County of Yanzhou in the names of the Tang (Zhengyi); modern Wenshang, Shandong.

pages.label: 247 BC · Ivar the Boneless' commentary and analysis I

entries.name: Liaocheng 聊城
entries.note: a Qi city on the lower Yellow River; a County of Bozhou in the names of the Tang (Zhengyi); modern Liaocheng, Shandong.

pages.label: 247 BC · Ivar the Boneless' commentary and analysis I

entries.name: Nanyang 南阳 (of Qi)
entries.note: Qi's southern lands, which the Suoyin takes as its lands north of the Huai and on the Si; distinct from Han's Nanyang.

pages.label: 247 BC · Ivar the Boneless' commentary and analysis I

entries.name: Jibei 济北
entries.note: the land north of the Ji River, the region of Liaocheng (Suoyin); modern north-western Shandong.

pages.label: 247 BC · Ivar the Boneless' commentary and analysis I

entries.name: Guan 管
entries.note: a Han town east of Zheng, the old Guan of the Zhou fief; modern Zhengzhou, Henan.

pages.label: 247 BC · Ivar the Boneless' commentary and analysis II

entries.name: Shang 商
entries.note: the Shang state and dynasty, with its late capital at Yin, modern Anyang, Henan.

entries.name: Ordos 鄂尔多斯
entries.note: the Ordos plateau within the great bend of the Yellow River; modern Ordos, Inner Mongolia.

entries.name: northern Shaanxi 陕北
entries.note: the loess highlands of northern Shaanxi, between the Ordos and the Wei valley.

entries.name: Guanzhong 关中
entries.note: the Wei River valley "within the passes", the heartland of Qin; modern central Shaanxi.

entries.name: Beicun, Yao County 耀县北村
entries.note: a Shang-culture site at Beicun in the former Yao County 耀县, since 2002 Yaozhou District 耀州区 of Tongchuan, Shaanxi.

entries.name: Yijiabu, Fufeng 扶风壹家堡
entries.note: a Shang-culture site at Yijiabu in Fufeng County, Baoji, Shaanxi.

entries.name: Wei River 渭水
entries.note: the Wei, the river of the Guanzhong, joining the Yellow River at Tongguan.

entries.name: Qishui River 漆水河
entries.note: a northern tributary of the Wei in central Shaanxi, flowing past Wugong and Fufeng.

entries.name: Zhouyuan 周原
entries.note: the Zhou plain north of the Wei, between Qishan and Fufeng, Shaanxi, the early seat of the Zhou.

entries.name: Binzhou 彬州
entries.note: Binzhou (formerly Bin County) on the Jing River, Xianyang, Shaanxi.

entries.name: Xunyi 旬邑
entries.note: Xunyi County on the upper Jing, Xianyang, Shaanxi, east of Binzhou.

entries.name: southern Shanxi 晋南
entries.note: the Fen and lower Qin valleys of southern Shanxi, west of the Taihang.

entries.name: Shijia site, Huantai 桓台史家遗址
entries.note: a Shang-period site at Shijia in Huantai County, Zibo, Shandong.

entries.name: Hua 画
entries.note: the fief of Zi Hua in the east, in modern Shandong.

entries.name: Tan 谭
entries.note: the state of Tan in the east; modern Zhangqiu, Jinan, Shandong.

entries.name: central Shanxi 晋中
entries.note: the Taiyuan basin and the uplands about it.

entries.name: Hanjiang 汉江
entries.note: the Han, the great northern tributary of the Yangtze, joining it at modern Wuhan.

entries.name: Nan Commandery 南郡
entries.note: Qin's Commandery on the old Chu capital region about Ying, set up in 278 BC; modern Jingzhou, Hubei.

entries.name: Hedong Commandery 河东郡
entries.note: Qin's Commandery east of the Yellow River's southward course, the old Wei lands of south-western Shanxi; modern Yuncheng.

entries.name: Lijiaya site, Qingjian 清涧李家崖遗址
entries.note: a walled site of the Late Shang period at Lijiaya, Qingjian County, Yulin, Shaanxi; the type site of the Lijiaya culture.

entries.name: Yin 殷
entries.note: the last capital of the Shang, to which Pan Geng moved; the site of Yinxu, at modern Anyang, Henan.

entries.name: Gaohong site, Liulin 柳林高红遗址
entries.note: a Late Shang-period site with large rammed-earth buildings at Gaohong, Liulin County, Lüliang, Shanxi.

entries.name: Jingjie, Lingshi 灵石旌介
entries.note: the Shang tombs at Jingjie, Lingshi County, Jinzhong, Shanxi.

entries.name: Qiaobei, Fushan 浮山桥北
entries.note: the Shang tombs at Qiaobei, Fushan County, Linfen, Shanxi.

entries.name: Bing 丙
entries.note: a state under the Shang king in central Shanxi, known from the bronze inscriptions of the Jingjie tombs at Lingshi.

entries.name: Xian 先
entries.note: a state under the Shang king in central Shanxi, known from the bronze inscriptions of the Qiaobei tombs at Fushan.

entries.name: South Korea 韩国
entries.note: the southern part of the Korean peninsula, the modern Republic of Korea.

entries.name: Xujianian site 徐家碾遗址
entries.note: a cemetery site of the Siwa culture at Xujianian, Zhuanglang County, Pingliang, Gansu.

entries.name: Chunhua 淳化
entries.note: Chunhua County, Xianyang, Shaanxi, on the northern edge of the Guanzhong.

entries.name: Bin 豳
entries.note: the seat of the Zhou before King Tai's move; traditionally placed about Xunyi and Binzhou, Shaanxi.

entries.name: Qi Zhou 岐周
entries.note: the seat of the Zhou at the foot of Mount Qi, in the Zhouyuan, from King Tai's move.

entries.name: Qishan 岐山
entries.note: the mountain north of the Zhouyuan; in Qishan County, Baoji, Shaanxi.

entries.name: Jing River 泾河
entries.note: a northern tributary of Wei River, joining it east of Xi'an.

entries.name: Yu 虞
entries.note: a Zhou state at Pinglu in southern Shanxi.

entries.name: Pinglu 平陆
entries.note: Pinglu County, Yuncheng, Shanxi, on the north bank of the Yellow River; not the Pinglu of Qi.

entries.name: Ganjiang 赣江
entries.note: the main river of Jiangxi, flowing north into Poyang Lake.

entries.name: Ning–Zhen region 宁镇地区
entries.note: the Nanjing–Zhenjiang area of south-western Jiangsu.

entries.name: Shao Fortress 召城
entries.note: the fief of Shi, Duke of Shao, in the first years of the Western Zhou; traditionally placed south-west of Qishan County, Shaanxi.

entries.name: northern Shandong 鲁北
entries.note: the plain of Shandong north of its central hills, along the Bohai.

entries.name: Mi River 弥河
entries.note: a river of north-central Shandong, flowing north past Qingzhou into the Bohai.

entries.name: Subutun cemetery, Qingzhou 青州苏埠屯墓葬群
entries.note: the Late Shang cemetery at Subutun, Qingzhou, Weifang, Shandong.

entries.name: Pugu 蒲姑
entries.note: a state of the east in the transmitted texts, also written 薄姑.

entries.name: Bohai 渤海
entries.note: the gulf enclosed by the Liaodong and Shandong peninsulas.

entries.name: Cangzhou 沧州
entries.note: Cangzhou, on the Bohai coast of south-eastern Hebei.

entries.name: Xi'an 西安
entries.note: the modern city of Xi'an, Shaanxi, in the middle of the Guanzhong.

entries.name: Shanxi–Shaanxi plateau 晋陕高原
entries.note: the loess uplands on both sides of the Yellow River between Shanxi and Shaanxi.

entries.name: Feng 丰
entries.note: Feng, named by the Rongchengshi among the states King Wen subdued; the settlement of Feng 丰邑 on Feng River 沣河, to which King Wen moved his capital, south-west of modern Xi'an, Shaanxi.

entries.name: You 攸
entries.note: a state lying close to the Yifang, in the oracle-bone inscriptions.

entries.name: Great Settlement Shang 大邑商
entries.note: the name the oracle-bone inscriptions give to the Shang king's seat in the royal domain.

entries.name: Wei 危
entries.note: a place reached by Di Xin on his march against the Yifang, in the oracle-bone inscriptions.

entries.name: Youli 羑里
entries.note: the place where King Wen was imprisoned; traditionally placed at Tangyin, Anyang, Henan.

entries.name: Rui 芮
entries.note: a small state neighbouring Yu; traditionally placed at Ruicheng, Shanxi, or at Dali, Shaanxi.

entries.name: Mixu 密须
entries.note: a state attacked and destroyed by King Wen; traditionally placed at Lingtai, Pingliang, Gansu.

entries.name: Qi 耆
entries.note: the state written 耆 in the Basic Annals of Zhou and the Qiye and 黎, Li, in the Documents and the Zuozhuan; traditionally placed about Licheng and Changzhi, Shanxi.

entries.name: Yu 邘
entries.note: a state attacked by King Wen; traditionally placed at Qinyang, Jiaozuo, Henan.

entries.name: Lü 吕
entries.note: a dependent state of Yin Shang in the Shanxi region.

entries.name: Chong 崇
entries.note: the state of Hu, Marquis of Chong, destroyed by King Wen; some scholars identify the Laoniupo site with it.

entries.name: Laoniupo site 老牛坡遗址
entries.note: a Shang-period site at Laoniupo, Baqiao District, Xi'an, Shaanxi.

entries.name: Hao 镐
entries.note: Hao, named by the Rongchengshi among the states King Wen subdued; Haojing 镐京, built under King Wu on Feng River opposite Feng, south-west of modern Xi'an, Shaanxi.

entries.name: Nuo 郍
entries.note: named by the Rongchengshi among the states King Wen subdued.

entries.name: Lu 鹿
entries.note: named by the Rongchengshi among the states King Wen subdued.

entries.name: Yi River 伊
entries.note: a tributary of Luo River in western Henan, flowing through Yique south of Luoyang.

entries.name: Luo River 洛
entries.note: a southern tributary of the Yellow River in western Henan, flowing past Luoyang.

entries.name: Meng Ford 盟津
entries.note: the ford of the Yellow River north of Luoyang, also written 孟津; modern Mengjin, Luoyang, Henan.

entries.name: Luoshi 洛师
entries.note: the land on Luo River about modern Luoyang, Henan; the 洛师 of the Documents.

entries.name: Zhaoge 朝歌
entries.note: the secondary capital of Yin Shang; modern Qi County 淇县, Hebi, Henan.

entries.name: Muye 牧野
entries.note: the ground outside Zhaoge where King Wu defeated Di Xin; south of modern Qi County, towards Xinxiang, Henan.

entries.name: Lu Terrace 鹿台
entries.note: the terrace of Di Xin at Zhaoge.

entries.name: Wei 微
entries.note: the fief of Weizi Qi; traditionally placed at Lucheng, Changzhi, Shanxi.

entries.name: Lanshi 阑师
entries.note: the place where King Wu was on the day Xinwei, seven days after the conquest, in the inscription of the Li gui.

entries.name: Chen 陈
entries.note: the state of the descendants of Shun; modern Huaiyang, Zhoukou, Henan.

entries.name: Qi 杞
entries.note: the state of the descendants of Xia; first at modern Qi County 杞县, Kaifeng, Henan.

entries.name: Bei 邶
entries.note: the land north of the Shang capital where Wu Geng was enfeoffed; traditionally placed at Tangyin, Anyang, Henan.

entries.name: Cao 曹
entries.note: a state of a brother of King Wu; modern Dingtao, Heze, Shandong.

entries.name: Gao 郜
entries.note: a state of a brother of King Wu; modern Chengwu, Heze, Shandong.

entries.name: Cheng 郕
entries.note: a state of a brother of King Wu; traditionally placed about Ningyang, Tai'an, Shandong.

entries.name: Yingqiu 营丘
entries.note: the first seat of the state of Qi, where Taigong was enfeoffed; traditionally placed at Linzi, Zibo, or at Changle, Weifang, Shandong.

entries.name: Malian River 马莲河
entries.note: a northern tributary of Jing River in eastern Gansu, flowing through Huan County, Heshui and Ning County.

entries.name: Lingtai 灵台
entries.note: Lingtai County, Pingliang, Gansu.

entries.name: Chongxin 崇信
entries.note: Chongxin County, Pingliang, Gansu.

entries.name: Ning County 宁县
entries.note: Ning County, Qingyang, Gansu.

entries.name: Heshui 合水
entries.note: Heshui County, Qingyang, Gansu.

entries.name: Huan County 环县
entries.note: Huan County, Qingyang, Gansu.

entries.name: Yan 奄
entries.note: a state of the east that sided with Wu Geng, also called Shang Yan 商奄; traditionally placed at Qufu, Jining, Shandong.

entries.name: Wen 温
entries.note: a state on the road south from the old Shang royal domain; modern Wen County, Jiaozuo, Henan.

entries.name: Tan 檀
entries.note: a state which, with Wen, held the road south from the old Shang royal domain to the Yi and Luo region.

entries.name: Yuan 原
entries.note: a state at the southern foot of Taihangshan; modern Jiyuan, Henan.

entries.name: Yong 雍
entries.note: a state at the southern foot of Taihangshan, about modern Jiaozuo, Henan; not the Yong of Qin.

entries.name: Taihangshan 太行山
entries.note: the range between the Shanxi plateau and the North China plain.

entries.name: Ji River 济水
entries.note: the old river that ran from the Yellow River about Xingyang east across western Shandong to the sea.

entries.name: Xiaotun 小屯
entries.note: the village at Anyang, Henan, at the centre of the Yinxu site, where the palace and temple foundations were excavated.

entries.name: Ji 㠱
entries.note: a state of the Beijing region in the bronze inscriptions, founded by Jizi's clan after its move north.

entries.name: Guzhu 孤竹
entries.note: a state north of Yan; traditionally placed about Lulong, Qinhuangdao, Hebei.

entries.name: Zhuyushan 朱圉山
entries.note: a mountain of eastern Gansu, in Gangu County, Tianshui.

entries.name: Feng 丰
entries.note: the Dongyi state of the Earl of Feng 丰伯, destroyed by the Duke of Zhou; not the Feng of King Wen.

entries.name: Ji 纪
entries.note: a state of the east; modern Shouguang, Weifang, Shandong.

entries.name: Xue 薛
entries.note: a state of the east; modern Tengzhou, Zaozhuang, Shandong.

entries.name: Xu 徐
entries.note: the great state of the Dongyi on the lower Huai; about modern Sihong, Suqian, Jiangsu.

entries.name: Jiubi 九毕
entries.note: the place near Luo, held by a strong force, to which the Duke of Zhou moved the old nobility of Yin Shang who had risen with Wu Geng.

entries.name: Luoyi 洛邑
entries.note: the new capital built by the Duke of Zhou on Luo River, called Chengzhou 成周; modern Luoyang, Henan.

entries.name: Xutian 许田
entries.note: a holding of the state of Lu near the capital of the state of Xu 许, the lodging of the rulers of Lu on their way to court.

entries.name: Lintong 临潼
entries.note: Lintong District, Xi'an, Shaanxi.

entries.name: Miji 靡集
entries.note: a place in the land of Chen attacked by Hou Lai after the conquest, in the Great Capture chapter of the Yi Zhou Shu.

entries.name: Wei 韦
entries.note: a place attacked by one of King Wu's commanders after the conquest, in the Great Capture chapter of the Yi Zhou Shu.

entries.name: Li 磿
entries.note: a place attacked by one of King Wu's commanders after the conquest, in the Great Capture chapter of the Yi Zhou Shu.

entries.name: Shu 蜀
entries.note: a place attacked by one of King Wu's commanders after the conquest, in the Great Capture chapter of the Yi Zhou Shu.

entries.name: Bi 毕
entries.note: the burial place of the Duke of Zhou, beside King Wen; traditionally placed south-west of Xi'an, near Feng and Hao, or on the upland north of Xianyang, Shaanxi.

entries.name: Yang 昜
entries.note: the first fief of Tangshu Yu as a bronze inscription writes it, the Tang 唐 of the transmitted texts; in southern Shanxi, traditionally placed at Yicheng, Linfen.

entries.name: Machanggou, Kazuo 喀左马厂沟村
entries.note: a village in Kazuo County, Chaoyang, Liaoning, where a hoard of early Western Zhou bronzes was found in 1955, among them the yu of the Marquis of Yan.

entries.name: Kuai 桧
entries.note: a state attacked in King Zhao's time, in the bronze inscriptions; taken as the Kuai of the transmitted texts, also written 郐, about Xinmi, Zhengzhou, Henan.

entries.name: Ru River 汝水
entries.note: a northern tributary of the Huai in central Henan.

entries.name: Ying River 颍水
entries.note: a northern tributary of the Huai, rising about Dengfeng, Henan, and joining the Huai in Anhui.

entries.name: Sha River 沙水
entries.note: a river of eastern Henan, a branch of the Ying; the modern Shahe joins Ying River at Zhoukou.

entries.name: Hu 胡
entries.note: a state of the Ying and Huai country where Dong fought the Huaiyi; traditionally placed at Yancheng, Luohe, Henan, or at Fuyang, Anhui.

entries.name: Quanqiu 犬丘
entries.note: the Zhou name of the Huaili 槐里 of Right Fufeng under the Han, the capital of King Yi 懿; modern Xingping, Xianyang, Shaanxi.

entries.name: Taiyuan 太原
entries.note: the Taiyuan to which King Mu moved the Quan Rong, in the Bamboo Annals; generally placed on the upper Jing River about Pingliang, Gansu, and Guyuan, Ningxia, not at the Taiyuan of Shanxi.

entries.name: Qin 秦
entries.note: the settlement given to Feizi by King Xiao of Zhou, from which the house of Qin took its name; traditionally placed about Qingshui and Zhangjiachuan, Tianshui, Gansu.

entries.name: E 噩
entries.note: a state of the south, written 噩 in the bronze inscriptions and 鄂 in the transmitted texts; its early Western Zhou cemetery lies at Yangzishan, Suizhou, Hubei.

entries.name: Xiaquan village 下泉村
entries.note: Xiaquan village, Chang'an District, Xi'an, Shaanxi, where the Duo You ding was found in 1980.

entries.name: Zhi 彘
entries.note: the place of King Li's exile; modern Huozhou, Linfen, Shanxi.

entries.name: 诸侯 the Lords
entries.note: the rulers of the states, collectively; in this period the kings of the warring states and the lesser lords, as distinct from the Zhou king.

entries.name: 霸 hegemon
entries.note: the lord who holds the leadership of the Lords.

entries.name: 君长 chieftain
entries.note: the head of a small or dependent people, below the rank of king.

entries.name: 衛戍病院 garrison hospital
entries.note: a military hospital of a garrison town.

entries.name: 旅 brigade
entries.note: the army unit of the period between regiment and division.

entries.name: 決死隊 death squad
entries.note: a party of volunteers for an assault from which return is not expected.

entries.name: 軍醫 army doctor
entries.note: a medical officer of the army.

entries.name: 滿鐵 the South Manchuria Railway
entries.note: the South Manchuria Railway Company (南滿洲鐵道), the Japanese railway concern in Manchuria.

entries.name: 赤十字 the Red Cross
entries.note: the Red Cross society.

entries.name: 渤海艦隊 the Bohai Fleet
entries.note: the naval squadron on the Zhili side in 1924, based at Qingdao and Qinhuangdao.

entries.name: 陸戰隊 marines
entries.note: a navy's landing force.

entries.name: 奉天軍 the Fengtian army
entries.note: the forces of the Fengtian clique; also written 奉軍.

entries.name: 副司令 deputy commander
entries.note: the second in command of an army.

entries.name: 旅長 brigade commander
entries.note: the officer commanding a brigade.

entries.name: 直隸軍 the Zhili army
entries.note: the forces of the Zhili clique; also written 直軍.

entries.name: 總司令 commander-in-chief
entries.note: the officer in supreme command.

entries.name: 内史 Clerk of the Capital
entries.note: the office governing the home territory of Qin about the capital.

pages.label: 249 BC · Qin slips in the Yuelu Academy collection

entries.name: 西工室 the Western Workshop
entries.note: a state workshop (工室) of Qin, staffed with convicts and men on labour service; the statute does not say where it stood. A Qin Western Workshop (西工) of Shu Commandery is attested on slips excavated at Zikujie, Chengdu.

pages.label: 249 BC · Qin slips in the Yuelu Academy collection

entries.name: 司寇 sikou
entries.note: the lightest grade of Qin convict labour, 'robber-guard', ranking between commoners and the lichenqie 隶臣妾 slaves; by Han law a term of two years.

pages.label: 249 BC · Qin slips in the Yuelu Academy collection

entries.name: 隐官 yinguan
entries.note: a person pardoned after a mutilating punishment and set to work out of public sight, 'the hidden'; a status ranked with the sikou.

pages.label: 249 BC · Qin slips in the Yuelu Academy collection

entries.name: 践更 serving one's geng turn
entries.note: performing in person one's turn (更) of statutory labour service for the government, as against hiring a substitute.

pages.label: 249 BC · Qin slips in the Yuelu Academy collection

entries.name: 五刑 the five punishments
entries.note: the five mutilating punishments of the ancient codes: tattooing, cutting off the nose, cutting off the feet, castration and death.

pages.label: 249 BC · Appendix: text of the Zhanguo Zonghengjia Shu

entries.name: 干将、莫邪 Ganjiang and Moye
entries.note: the two swords of legend, forged for the King of Wu by the smith Ganjiang and his wife Moye; the type of a fine blade.

pages.label: 249 BC · Appendix: text of the Zhanguo Zonghengjia Shu

entries.name: 騄耳 Lü'er
entries.note: one of the eight steeds of King Mu of Zhou; the type of a fine horse.

pages.label: 249 BC · Appendix: text of the Zhanguo Zonghengjia Shu

entries.name: 谈说之士 persuaders
entries.note: the itinerant counsellors who sold rulers plans of war and alliance.

pages.label: 249 BC · Appendix: text of the Zhanguo Zonghengjia Shu

entries.name: 仲父 Second Father
entries.note: the style a ruler gave a minister honoured as a father, after Duke Huan of Qi's for Guan Zhong (Zhengyi).

entries.name: 家僮 household slaves
entries.note: the bondsmen of a great house.

entries.name: 辩士 disputant
entries.note: a master of argument; a travelling rhetorician.

entries.name: 腐 castration
entries.note: the palace punishment, 宫刑; 腐罪, an offence punished by it.

entries.name: 给事中 palace attendant
entries.note: one attending within the palace.

entries.name: 宦者 eunuch
entries.note: a castrated servant of the palace.

entries.name: 郎 Court Gentleman
entries.note: a court attendant of the king's entourage; the office, as distinct from 士, the gentlemen as a class.

entries.name: 长史 Senior Clerk
entries.note: the chief secretary of a minister or office.

entries.name: 五帝 the Five Emperors
entries.note: the sage rulers before the Three Kings.

entries.name: 黔首 the black-headed people
entries.note: the common people, the Qin term.

entries.name: 廷尉 Commandant of Justice
entries.note: the chief judicial officer of Qin.

entries.name: 皇帝 Emperor
entries.note: the title the King of Qin took in 221 BC.

entries.name: 陛下 Your Majesty
entries.note: the address to the ruler, literally "beneath the steps".

entries.name: 后宫 harem
entries.note: the women's quarters of the palace, literally the "rear palace".

entries.name: 六国 the Six States
entries.note: Han, Zhao, Wei, Chu, Yan and Qi, the eastern states facing Qin.

entries.name: 关东 east of the Pass
entries.note: the lands east of Hangu Pass, the eastern states.

entries.name: 九夷 the Nine Yi
entries.note: the Yi peoples of Chu's lands (Suoyin); a set phrase for the southern peoples.

entries.name: 中商 Middle Shang
entries.note: the middle period of Shang archaeology, between the Erligang and Yinxu periods.

entries.name: 殷墟一期 Yinxu Phase I
entries.note: the first of the four phases of the Yinxu (Anyang) period, corresponding to the reigns of Pan Geng to Wu Ding.

entries.name: 朱开沟 Zhukaigou
entries.note: the Bronze Age culture of the Ordos named from the Zhukaigou site, Ejin Horo Banner, and the people who bore it.

entries.name: 蛇纹鬲 snake-pattern li
entries.note: the li tripod with applied snake-like strips, the type vessel of the Zhukaigou culture.

entries.name: 方 fang state
entries.note: the polities around the Shang, so named in the oracle-bone inscriptions.

entries.name: 犬方 the Quanfang
entries.note: a fang state of the west against which Wu Ding sent armies.

entries.name: 周方 the Zhoufang
entries.note: the Zhou as a fang state in the oracle-bone inscriptions.

entries.name: 甲骨卜辞 oracle-bone inscriptions
entries.note: the divination records of the Shang kings on turtle plastron and ox bone.

entries.name: 郑家坡文化 Zhengjiapo culture
entries.note: the late Shang-period culture of the Qishui valley named from the Zhengjiapo site, Wugong, Shaanxi.

entries.name: 京当型 Jingdang type
entries.note: the local type of Shang culture in the Zhouyuan region, named from the Jingdang site, Fufeng.

entries.name: 孙家类型 Sunjia type
entries.note: the cultural type of the upper Jing valley named from the Sunjia site, Binzhou.

entries.name: 先周文化 Proto-Zhou culture
entries.note: the archaeological culture of the Zhou before the conquest of Shang.

entries.name: 西土 the western lands
entries.note: the lands west of the Shang, as the oracle-bone inscriptions call them.

entries.name: 方方 the Fang
entries.note: the fang state named Fang 方 in the oracle-bone inscriptions, a people of the north-west under Wu Ding.

entries.name: 亘方 the Gengfang
entries.note: a fang state west of Yin, in southern Shanxi, conquered by Wu Ding; written 亙方 in some lists.

entries.name: 缶 Fou
entries.note: the state of Fou (缶方) west of Yin, conquered by Wu Ding.

entries.name: 基方 the Jifang
entries.note: a fang state west of Yin, placed at modern Puxian, Shanxi, conquered by Wu Ding.

entries.name: 湔方 the Jianfang
entries.note: a fang state west of Yin, in the Shanxi–Shaanxi uplands, conquered by Wu Ding.

entries.name: 晚商 Late Shang
entries.note: the Yinxu period of Shang archaeology, from Pan Geng's move to Yin.

entries.name: 沚方 the Zhifang
entries.note: a fang state west of Yin, bordering the Qiongfang; conquered by Wu Ding, its chief Zhi Guo then his vassal.

entries.name: 辔方 the Peifang
entries.note: a fang state west of Yin, bordering the Qiongfang, attacked by Wu Ding and Que.

entries.name: 𢀛方 the Qiongfang
entries.note: the most persistent enemy of Wu Ding's Shang, north-west of Yin in the Shanxi–Shaanxi uplands, often allied with the Tufang; the graph 𢀛, 工 over 口, is also transcribed 工方.

entries.name: 戉 Yue
entries.note: a polity or leader in the west that revolted early in Wu Ding's reign and was put down by Que.

entries.name: 巴方 the Bafang
entries.note: a fang state in Shanxi, attacked under Wu Ding.

entries.name: 土方 the Tufang
entries.note: a fang state north-west of Yin, east of the Qiongfang, in the Fen valley of Shanxi; defeated by Wu Ding.

entries.name: 夷方 the Yifang
entries.note: a fang state of the east, against which Fu Zi campaigned.

entries.name: 龙方 the Longfang
entries.note: a fang state west of Yin, against which Fu Geng campaigned.

entries.name: 石楼类型 Shilou type
entries.note: the late Shang bronze-bearing remains of the Shanxi–Shaanxi uplands named from Shilou County, Shanxi, which some connect with the Qiongfang.

entries.name: 铜路 the copper road
entries.note: the route by which copper and other bronze metals reached Yin from the south.

entries.name: 虎方 the Hufang
entries.note: a fang state of the south, attacked in Wu Ding's southern expedition; identified by different scholars with the Miaotaizi type, the Dachengdun type or the Wucheng culture.

entries.name: 方 the Moufang
entries.note: a fang state of the south, attacked by Wu Ding and Wang Cheng and thereafter unrecorded; its graph, 中 with a doubled vertical stroke, has no code point and is drawn.

entries.name: 魏营子文化 Weiyingzi culture
entries.note: the late Shang to early Western Zhou culture of the western Liao valley named from the Weiyingzi site, Chaoyang, Liaoning.

entries.name: 夏家店下层文化 Lower Xiajiadian culture
entries.note: the early Bronze Age culture of the western Liao valley and the Yan hills, named from the lower stratum of the Xiajiadian site, Chifeng, Inner Mongolia.

entries.name: 围坊三期文化 Weifang Phase III culture
entries.note: the culture of the Tianjin–northern Hebei plain named from the third phase of the Weifang site, Jizhou, Tianjin.

entries.name: 围坊类型 Weifang type
entries.note: a type of the Weifang Phase III culture, its late Shang form on the Tianjin–northern Hebei plain.

entries.name: 庙台子类型 Miaotaizi type
entries.note: a late Shang cultural type of the middle Yangtze named from the Miaotaizi site; one of the cultures identified with the Hufang.

entries.name: 大城墩类型 Dachengdun type
entries.note: a Shang-period cultural type of the Jianghuai region named from the Dachengdun site, Hanshan, Anhui.

entries.name: 吴城文化 Wucheng culture
entries.note: the Shang-period bronze culture of the Gan valley named from the Wucheng site, Zhangshu, Jiangxi.

entries.name: 路家河文化 Lujiahe culture
entries.note: the Shang-period culture of the Yangtze gorges named from the Lujiahe site, Yichang, Hubei.

entries.name: 石地坝文化 Shidiba culture
entries.note: the Shang-period culture of the Yangtze above the gorges named from the Shidiba site, Zhongxian, Chongqing.

entries.name: 周梁玉桥文化 Zhouliangyuqiao culture
entries.note: the Shang-period culture of the Jianghan plain named from the Zhouliangyuqiao site, Shashi, Jingzhou, Hubei.

entries.name: 殷墟二期 Yinxu Phase II
entries.note: the second of the four phases of the Yinxu (Anyang) period, its early stage corresponding to the middle and later part of Wu Ding's reign.

entries.name: 羌方 the Qiangfang
entries.note: the Qiang as a fang state of the west in the oracle-bone inscriptions.

entries.name: 刘家文化 Liujia culture
entries.note: the Late Shang-period culture of the western Guanzhong named from the Liujia cemetery, Fufeng, Shaanxi; regarded by many scholars as the culture of the Qiangfang.

entries.name: 李家崖文化 Lijiaya culture
entries.note: the Late Shang-period culture of northern Shaanxi and the facing bank of the Yellow River, named from the Lijiaya site, Qingjian, Shaanxi.

entries.name: 西岔文化 Xicha culture
entries.note: a culture of the Late Shang period named from the Xicha site, Qingshuihe County, Inner Mongolia.

entries.name: 陶文 pottery inscriptions
entries.note: graphs incised or written on pottery.

entries.name: 鬼方 the Guifang
entries.note: a people of the north-west in the oracle-bone inscriptions and the Zhouyi, attacked by Gaozong (Wu Ding).

entries.name: 大城墩四期文化 Dachengdun Phase IV culture
entries.note: the culture named from the fourth phase of the Dachengdun site, Hanshan, Anhui.

entries.name: 小白阳类型 Xiaobaiyang type
entries.note: a type of the Weiyingzi culture, named from the Xiaobaiyang site.

entries.name: 石灰山文化 Shihuishan culture
entries.note: a culture that existed beside the Wucheng culture and then merged into it, named from the Shihuishan site.

entries.name: 日名 day name
entries.note: the heavenly-stem name (甲, 乙 … 癸) by which a Shang royal ancestor is called in sacrifice.

entries.name: 周祭制度 cyclical sacrifice system
entries.note: the fixed round of sacrifices offered in turn to the royal ancestors of the Shang, each on the day of his or her stem name.

entries.name: 贞人 diviners
entries.note: the officers who put the charge to the oracle in the divination inscriptions.

entries.name: 美沙里类型 Misa-ri type
entries.note: the earliest Bronze Age pottery type of central-western Korea, named from the site of Misa-ri (美沙里, Meishali in pinyin), Hanam, Gyeonggi.

entries.name: 可乐洞 Garak-dong
entries.note: the pottery type and stage of the Korean Early Bronze Age named from Garak-dong (可乐洞, Keledong in pinyin), Seoul.

entries.name: 欣岩里 Heunam-ri
entries.note: the pottery type and stage of the Korean Early Bronze Age named from Heunam-ri (欣岩里, Xinyanli in pinyin), Yeoju, Gyeonggi.

entries.name: 驿三洞 Yeoksam-dong
entries.note: the pottery type and stage of the Korean Early Bronze Age named from Yeoksam-dong (驿三洞, Yisandong in pinyin), Seoul.

entries.name: 虎谷洞二期文化 Beomui-guseok Phase II culture
entries.note: the culture named from the second phase of the Beomui-guseok site (虎谷洞, Hugudong in pinyin), Musan, North Hamgyong.

entries.name: 寺洼文化 Siwa culture
entries.note: the Bronze Age culture of eastern Gansu named from Siwashan, Lintao, Gansu.

entries.name: 枣树沟脑类型 Zaoshugounao type
entries.note: a type of remains in the Chunhua region named from the Zaoshugounao site, formed as late Zhukaigou and Lijiaya elements blended with the cultures of Guanzhong.

entries.name: 黑豆嘴类型 Heidouzui type
entries.note: a type of remains in the Chunhua region named from the Heidouzui site, formed as late Zhukaigou and Lijiaya elements blended with the cultures of Guanzhong.

entries.name: 薰鬻戎狄 the Xunyu Rong and Di
entries.note: the Xunyu, the northern people who in the transmitted texts pressed on the Zhou under King Tai; written 薰育 in the Basic Annals of Zhou and 獯鬻 in the Mencius.

entries.name: 青海青铜文化 Bronze Age cultures of Qinghai
entries.note: the Bronze Age cultures of Qinghai taken together; not a single culture.

entries.name: 张家园上层文化 Upper Zhangjiayuan culture
entries.note: the culture named from the upper stratum of the Zhangjiayuan site, Jizhou, Tianjin.

entries.name: 戍 garrison
entries.note: shu, the garrison units of the Shang army in the oracle-bone inscriptions.

entries.name: 行 column
entries.note: hang, a formation of the Shang army in the oracle-bone inscriptions.

entries.name: 危方 the Weifang
entries.note: a fang state of the south-east, attacked by Kang Ding.

entries.name: 虘方 the Cuofang
entries.note: a fang state of the west, friendly after Wu Ding's campaigns and hostile again under Kang Ding.

entries.name: 絴方 the Xiangfang
entries.note: a fang state of the west, hostile under Kang Ding, which submitted under Wu Yi.

entries.name: 兹方 the Zifang
entries.note: a fang state of the west, friendly after Wu Ding's campaigns and hostile again under Kang Ding.

entries.name: 碾子坡类型 Nianzipo type
entries.note: a type of remains on the middle and upper Jing River named from the Nianzipo site, Changwu, Shaanxi.

entries.name: 断泾二期 Duanjing Phase II
entries.note: the remains named from the second phase of the Duanjing site, Binzhou, Shaanxi.

entries.name: 召方 the Shaofang
entries.note: a fang state of the west attacked by Wu Yi.

entries.name: 殷墟三期 Yinxu Phase III
entries.note: the third of the four phases of the Yinxu (Anyang) period.

entries.name: 珍珠门文化 Zhenzhumen culture
entries.note: the native culture of northern Shandong in the Late Shang period, named from the Zhenzhumen site, Changdao, Shandong.

entries.name: 毕程氏 the Bicheng clan
entries.note: a people on Wei River destroyed by Jili, in the transmitted texts.

entries.name: 戎狄 the Rong and Di
entries.note: the non-Zhou peoples of the west and north in the transmitted texts.

entries.name: 鬼戎 the Gui Rong
entries.note: a Rong people attacked by Jili; the 西落鬼戎 of the Bamboo Annals.

entries.name: 燕京戎 the Yanjing Rong
entries.note: a Rong people against whom Jili was defeated; the 燕京之戎 of the Bamboo Annals.

entries.name: 余无之戎 the Rong of Yuwu
entries.note: a Rong people defeated by Jili.

entries.name: 牧师 mushi
entries.note: the title conferred on Jili by Wen Ding, in the Bamboo Annals.

entries.name: 九站类型 Jiuzhan type
entries.note: a type of the Siwa culture, named from the Jiuzhan site, Heshui, Gansu.

entries.name: 寺洼山类型 Siwashan type
entries.note: a type of the Siwa culture, named from Siwashan, Lintao, Gansu.

entries.name: 双房文化 Shuangfang culture
entries.note: the Bronze Age culture of the Liaodong peninsula named from the Shuangfang site, Pulandian, Liaoning.

entries.name: 新城子文化 Xinchengzi culture
entries.note: the Bronze Age culture named from the Xinchengzi site, Benxi, Liaoning.

entries.name: 于家上层文化 Upper Yujia culture
entries.note: the culture named from the upper stratum of the Yujiacun site, Lüshun, Liaoning.

entries.name: 马城子文化 Machengzi culture
entries.note: the Bronze Age culture named from the Machengzi caves, Benxi, Liaoning.

entries.name: 新岩里二期文化 Sinam-ri Phase II culture
entries.note: the culture named from the second phase of the Sinam-ri site (新岩里, Xinyanli in pinyin), in north-western Korea.

entries.name: 金滩里青铜时代一期文化 Geumtan-ri Bronze Age Phase I culture
entries.note: the culture named from the first Bronze Age phase of the Geumtan-ri site (金滩里, Jintanli in pinyin), at Pyongyang.

entries.name: 虎谷洞三期文化 Beomui-guseok Phase III culture
entries.note: the culture named from the third phase of the Beomui-guseok site (虎谷洞, Hugudong in pinyin), Musan, North Hamgyong.

entries.name: 三星堆四期文化 Sanxingdui Phase IV culture
entries.note: the culture named from the fourth phase of the Sanxingdui site.

entries.name: 三星堆文化 Sanxingdui culture
entries.note: the Bronze Age culture of the Chengdu plain named from the Sanxingdui site, Guanghan, Sichuan.

entries.name: 辛店文化 Xindian culture
entries.note: the Bronze Age culture of the upper Yellow River in Gansu and Qinghai named from the Xindian site, Lintao, Gansu.

entries.name: 殷墟四期 Yinxu Phase IV
entries.note: the last of the four phases of the Yinxu (Anyang) period, opening with the accession of Di Yi.

entries.name: 盂方 the Yufang
entries.note: a fang state against which Di Yi campaigned.

entries.name: 淮夷文化 Huaiyi culture
entries.note: the culture of the Huai River region that followed the Dachengdun Phase IV culture.

entries.name: 宰椃角 Zai Hao jiao
entries.note: a bronze jiao of the end of Shang, made for the steward (宰) Hao 椃, whose inscription is dated to the king's twenty-fifth si.

entries.name: 东夷 the Dongyi
entries.note: the Yi peoples of the east, in the transmitted texts.

entries.name: 金文 bronze inscriptions
entries.note: inscriptions cast or cut on bronze vessels.

entries.name: 祀 si
entries.note: the ritual year of the late Shang kings, a full round of the cyclical sacrifices, by which they counted the years of a reign.

entries.name: 王畿 royal domain
entries.note: the land about the capital under the king's own rule.

entries.name: 告祭 announcement sacrifice
entries.note: a sacrifice at which an undertaking is announced to the ancestors.

entries.name: 林方 the Linfang
entries.note: a fang state conquered by Di Xin on his campaign of the tenth si.

entries.name: 小臣艅犀尊 rhinoceros zun of the Lesser Minister Yu
entries.note: a bronze zun in the shape of a rhinoceros, of the end of Shang, with an inscription of twenty-seven characters; now in the Asian Art Museum, San Francisco.

entries.name: 小臣 Lesser Minister
entries.note: xiaochen, an official in the king's personal service.

entries.name: 黄组卜辞 Huang-group inscriptions
entries.note: the latest group of the Yinxu oracle-bone inscriptions, named from the diviner Huang 黄.

entries.name: 西伯 Chief of the West
entries.note: the title King Wen held under Di Xin.

entries.name: 受命 receiving the Mandate
entries.note: the receiving of the Mandate of Heaven to rule, claimed for King Wen.

entries.name: 犬戎 the Quan Rong
entries.note: a Rong people attacked by King Wen.

entries.name: 上博楚简 Shanghai Museum Chu slips
entries.note: the Warring States bamboo manuscripts of Chu held by the Shanghai Museum.

entries.name: 清华简 Tsinghua slips
entries.note: the Warring States bamboo manuscripts held by Tsinghua University.

entries.name: 虎贲 Tiger Braves
entries.note: huben, the picked warriors of the king's guard.

entries.name: 利簋 Li gui
entries.note: a bronze gui of the first years of the Western Zhou, unearthed at Lintong, Shaanxi, in 1976; its inscription dates the conquest of Shang to the morning of the day Jiazi.

entries.name: 越戏方 the Yuexifang
entries.note: a fang state attacked by Lü Ta on King Wu's orders, in the Great Capture chapter of the Yi Zhou Shu.

entries.name: 宣方 the Xuanfang
entries.note: a fang state attacked by Bai Wei on King Wu's orders, in the Great Capture chapter of the Yi Zhou Shu.

entries.name: 先代之后 descendants of the former dynasties
entries.note: the heirs of earlier ruling houses, enfeoffed by King Wu.

entries.name: 三恪 Three Ke
entries.note: the three houses of former dynasties enfeoffed and honoured by the Zhou: the descendants of Shun, of Xia and of Yin.

entries.name: 三监 Three Guards
entries.note: the three brothers of King Wu set to watch over the people of Yin: Guanshu, Caishu and Huoshu.

entries.name: 莱夷 the Laiyi
entries.note: the Yi people of the Shandong peninsula.

entries.name: 东土 the eastern lands
entries.note: the lands east of the Zhou homeland.

entries.name: 太保 Grand Guardian
entries.note: one of the highest offices of the early Zhou court, held by the Duke of Shao.

entries.name: 顽民 refractory people
entries.note: the people of Yin who had resisted the rule of Zhou and were moved to Luoyi.

entries.name: 司寇 Minister of Justice
entries.note: the Zhou office in charge of punishments.

entries.name: 奴虘之戎 the Rong of Nucuo
entries.note: a Rong people of the west, in the Xinian.

entries.name: 熊盈族 the Xiong and Ying clans
entries.note: peoples of the Dongyi conquered by the Duke of Zhou, in the Yi Zhou Shu.

entries.name: 夏家店上层文化 Upper Xiajiadian culture
entries.note: the Bronze Age culture of the western Liao valley named from the upper stratum of the Xiajiadian site, Chifeng, Inner Mongolia.

entries.name: 高台山文化 Gaotaishan culture
entries.note: the Bronze Age culture of the lower Liao valley named from the Gaotaishan site, Xinmin, Liaoning.

entries.name: 十二台营子文化 Shi'ertaiyingzi culture
entries.note: the Bronze Age culture named from the Shi'ertaiyingzi tombs, Chaoyang, Liaoning.

entries.name: 保德类型 Baode type
entries.note: the bronze-bearing remains of the Shanxi–Shaanxi uplands named from Baode County, Shanxi.

entries.name: 栏桥-徐家碾类型 Lanqiao–Xujianian type
entries.note: a type of the Siwa culture, named from the Lanqiao site, Xihe, and the Xujianian site, Zhuanglang, Gansu.

entries.name: 西团山文化 Xituanshan culture
entries.note: the Bronze Age culture of central Jilin named from the Xituanshan site, Jilin City.

entries.name: 宝山文化 Baoshan culture
entries.note: the Bronze Age culture of the upper Hanjiang valley named from the Baoshan site, Chenggu, Shaanxi.

entries.name: 炭河里文化 Tanheli culture
entries.note: the Bronze Age culture of the Xiang valley named from the Tanheli site, Ningxiang, Hunan.

entries.name: 万发拨子遗存 Wanfabozi remains
entries.note: the remains named from the Wanfabozi site, Tonghua, Jilin.

entries.name: 过伯簋 Guo Bo gui
entries.note: a bronze gui of the reign of King Zhao, cast by the Earl of Guo after following the King against Jing.

entries.name: 六师 six armies
entries.note: the royal army of the Zhou king.

entries.name: 淮夷 the Huaiyi
entries.note: the Yi peoples of the Huai region.

entries.name: 南夷 the Nanyi
entries.note: the Yi peoples of the south, in the bronze inscriptions.

entries.name: 卡约文化 Kayue culture
entries.note: the Bronze Age culture of eastern Qinghai named from the Kayue site, Huangzhong, Xining.

entries.name: 美松里上层文化 Upper Misong-ri culture
entries.note: the culture named from the upper stratum of the Misong-ri cave site (美松里, Meisongli in pinyin), Uiju, North Pyongan.

entries.name: 金滩里青铜文化 Geumtan-ri Bronze Age culture
entries.note: the Bronze Age culture named from the Geumtan-ri site (金滩里, Jintanli in pinyin), at Pyongyang.

entries.name: 班簋 Ban gui
entries.note: a bronze gui of the reign of King Mu, cast by Ban, whose inscription records three years of campaigning in the eastern states.

entries.name: 大小盂鼎 Da Yu ding and Xiao Yu ding
entries.note: two bronze ding cast by Yu; the Xiao Yu ding records his campaigns against the Guifang and the presentation of the captives.

entries.name: 史密簋 Shi Mi gui
entries.note: a bronze gui cast by Shi Mi, recording an eastern campaign with the army of Qi against the Nanyi and their allies; found at Ankang, Shaanxi, in 1986.

entries.name: 南淮夷 the Southern Huaiyi
entries.note: the Huaiyi of the south, in the bronze inscriptions, where 夷 is written 尸.

entries.name: 敔簋 Yu gui
entries.note: a bronze gui cast by Yu, recording his pursuit of the Southern Huaiyi.

entries.name: 鄂侯驭方鼎 E Hou Yufang ding
entries.note: a bronze ding cast by Yufang, Marquis of E, recording his reception by the King on the return from a southern campaign.

entries.name: 南京青铜时代二期文化 Namgyeong Bronze Age Phase II culture
entries.note: the culture named from the second Bronze Age phase of the Namgyeong site (南京, Nanjing in pinyin), at Pyongyang.

entries.name: 金滩里青铜时代二期文化 Geumtan-ri Bronze Age Phase II culture
entries.note: the culture named from the second Bronze Age phase of the Geumtan-ri site (金滩里, Jintanli in pinyin), at Pyongyang.

entries.name: 虎骨洞四期文化 Beomui-guseok Phase IV culture
entries.note: the culture named from the fourth phase of the Beomui-guseok site (虎谷洞, Hugudong in pinyin), Musan, North Hamgyong.

entries.name: 松菊里文化区 Songguk-ri culture area
entries.note: the area of the Songguk-ri culture, named from the Songguk-ri site (松菊里, Songjuli in pinyin), Buyeo, South Chungcheong.

entries.name: 禹鼎 Yu ding
entries.note: a bronze ding cast by Yu 禹, recording Duke Wu's campaign against Yufang, Marquis of E, and his capture.

entries.name: 宗周钟 Zongzhou zhong
entries.note: a bronze bell of King Li, recording his campaign against Fuzi of the southern lands and the audience of the Nanyi and the Dongyi.

entries.name: 多友鼎 Duo You ding
entries.note: a bronze ding cast by Duo You, recording the pursuit of the Xianyun who had raided towards the capital.

entries.name: 玁狁 the Xianyun
entries.note: a people of the north-west who raided the Zhou in the later Western Zhou.

entries.name: 荒服 Wild Domain
entries.note: the outermost of the five domains of submission, whose peoples owed the king tribute.

entries.name: 国人 people of the capital
entries.note: guoren, the free inhabitants of the capital, who paid the military levy, served as soldiers and were consulted on great matters of state.

entries.name: 共和 Gonghe
entries.note: the name of the fourteen years between King Li's flight and King Xuan's accession, 841–828 BC.

entries.name: 西戎 the Western Rong
entries.note: the Rong peoples west of the Zhou.
